records.text: Frank Turek said no CPR was performed during most of the ride to the hospital, but he tried CPR for about 20 or 30 seconds at the very end.
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: No, the truth of the matter is that going from that site to the hospital, we weren't doing CPR. ... We were trying to stop the bleeding. It was only in the last 20 or 30 seconds of the ride. ... So for the last 20 or 30 seconds, I tried to give him CPR. ... Is, I mean, Brian (Brian Harpole)'s generally right. No, we weren't doing CPR. I just tried it in the last few seconds, the last 20 to 30 seconds.

Brian (Brian Harpole) is correct that most of the ride we weren't doing any CPR. We couldn't do CPR. We're trying to stop the bleeding. ... So no CPR was done. It wasn't until the last, say, 30 seconds of the ride that I thought to myself. ... We got to be near in like eight or nine minutes and he's not breathing and there's no heartbeat. ... I've got to at least try. It's probably going to be futile, but I got to at least try to start his heart and get some air in him. ... So I tried that for like 20 or 30 seconds at the very end of the ride when we're pulling into the hospital parking lot and we're yanking and banking our way there.

Brian (Brian Harpole) is correct that most of the ride, we weren't doing any CPR. We couldn't do CPR. We're trying to stop the bleeding. ... So I tried that for like 20 or 30 seconds at the very end of the ride when we're pulling into the hospital parking lot and we're yanking and banking our way there.

verification.notes: The source-scoped transcript directly records Frank Turek saying most of the ride involved no CPR and that he attempted it during the final 20-30 seconds. Earlier public accounts also record Turek saying he called for CPR. This verifies what Turek said in the later clarification, not whether the attempted CPR occurred as described.

records.text: Turek Narrows CPR to Final Seconds
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: Brian (Brian Harpole) is correct that most of the ride, we weren't doing any CPR. We couldn't do CPR. We're trying to stop the bleeding. ... So I tried that for like 20 or 30 seconds at the very end of the ride when we're pulling into the hospital parking lot and we're yanking and banking our way there.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Turek refines his CPR account: no CPR occurred during most of the drive, but he says he tried it for roughly twenty to thirty seconds as the SUV reached the hospital.

records.text: Owens Says One CPR Witness Lied
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I think it's a lie. And you're now conceding that you lied or Brian (Brian Harpole) lied. I don't know who lied.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens rejects Turek's reconciliation and says either he or Harpole lied about CPR, while acknowledging she does not know which.

records.text: CPR Lie Accusation Is Not Plot Proof
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I think it's a lie. And you're now conceding that you lied or Brian (Brian Harpole) lied. I don't know who lied.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens's inability to identify which account is false leaves mistake, timing, terminology, perception, and intentional deception unresolved; none alone proves assassination participation.

records.text: Turek disputes CPR relevance
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: And so that's an incongruity. They're in on it then. Whether or not I did CPR has no bearing on who killed Charlie Kirk.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: In the replayed interview, Turek argued that whether he performed CPR had no bearing on who killed Kirk.

records.text: Owens cites lawsuit relevance
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's an irrelevant consequence. But it feels very relevant, actually. It's definitely relevant for me. I mean, I got Brian Harpole suing me on the basis of saying that he was just did all this upstanding care. ... So it's even more relevant to me than it is to other people. I know, as Bobby (Bobby Sausalito) pointed out, we are not and we have never suggested that you murdered Charlie (Charlie Kirk), but we have revealed that the people that were around Charlie (Charlie Kirk) in his final days have told a lot of lies since the very beginning of this thing.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens argued that the CPR dispute was particularly relevant to her because Harpole was suing her over his claimed upstanding care.

records.text: Hospital captain omission alleged
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But there's a major problem, you guys, a major problem. When I combine these two stories, which are running in conflict of one another, nowhere in Brian (Brian Harpole) or Frank (Frank Turek)'s extraordinary recounting of what happened on that day did either of them feature a fire captain who met them at the hospital and began performing CPR on Charlie (Charlie Kirk). ... That is an unbelievable oversight. Unbelievable as in I don't believe it. How could they both forget that? ... Two of them forgetting that detail registers to me as impossible. So, ladies and gentlemen, there is a fire captain that isn't barking.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens adds the allegation that both Turek’s and Harpole’s emergency-care accounts omit a fire captain who performed CPR at the hospital, saying she disbelieves that both forgot him.

records.text: Report describes hospital CPR
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #14 (Ep bIuvTKlFeGo)

appearances.snippet: 'Fire personnel from Station 1 and Station 3 were initially dispatched to the scene of the shooting. Personnel from Stations 2 and 4 also responded' ... because the extent of medical need was not yet known, while en route, the Station 3 fire truck passed near the SUV being used by the TPUSA security team to transport Charlie Kirk to Timpanogos Hospital. Station 3 personnel provided that information over the radio. ... Station 2 then rerouted Timpanogos Hospital. where the fire captain from Station 2 assisted in providing CPR to Charlie Kirk at the hospital.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The UVU review, quoted by Owens, says Station 3 radioed the security SUV’s movement and Station 2 rerouted to Timpanogos, where its captain assisted with CPR.

records.text: Book repeats CPR claim
records.speaker: Frank Turek

appearances.snippet: All three of us were in the back are still trying to stop the bleeding. I switch to CPR.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: In the book excerpt read by Owens, Turek says all three rear occupants were still trying to stop bleeding and that he switched to CPR.

records.text: Book omission challenged
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's not in a published book. You had no recall or mention of a fire captain doing CPR, which was revealed by the independent review. ... Nobody else remembers, but you curiously leave out the fire captain. Who's the fire captain? Who is the fire captain?

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens extends her hospital-captain omission allegation to Turek's newly presented book account, contrasting his personal CPR claim with its alleged lack of mention of the captain identified by the independent review.

records.text: Captain candidates narrowed
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Regarding Timpanogos, again, if you know who the fire chief was, the fire captain, pardon me, fire captain that administered CPR to Charlie (Charlie Kirk) at the hospital, please, we would like to hear from you. ... So we can confirm we are down to two possibilities, but we want an absolute confirmation. You can email us moretips at candaceowens.com.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens reports narrowing the hospital CPR captain's identity to two possibilities and asks for absolute confirmation rather than naming either.
